transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well... I suppose things have just been off lately. At the warehouse where I work. They, uh... they changed my hours around. Put in a new inventory system. 

I just... I guess I'm not handling it. I've been missing shifts. Missing church, too. Snapping at my family. Some mornings I just get dressed and... I just sit there in my work boots. Just wondering if I can even face going in. 

So, I guess that's why I'm here.
Can you tell me how you've been feeling emotionally lately, especially in the mornings when you're getting ready for work?

I don't really know. Emotionally, I mean. 

I guess I'm not really sure how to put it. I just... I feel tired, mostly. Like I said, I just sit there looking at my boots. I don't really have a word for it.
Do you usually feel down or depressed in the mornings, or most of the time, not just when you're getting ready for work?

I haven't really thought about it like that. I wouldn't call it... depressed. 

I just know it's hard when I have to put those boots on. The rest of the day... I don't know. I guess I don't really pay much attention.
When you're not getting ready for work, do you find yourself feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

I don't know... I mean, I told you I haven't been going to church as much. But I don't really sit around thinking about if I'm... down. I just do what I have to do around the house. It's just... I just don't feel much like doing anything else.
Can you think of a time recently when things weren’t stressful at work—maybe on a weekend or a day off—where you still felt down or low, not just tired?
I'm not sure. I don't really... keep track of things like that. Weekends are just weekends. I just try to rest up.
Can you remember if you’ve felt down or lost interest in things you used to enjoy, even when things weren’t stressful at work—like on your days off?

I... I don't really know what else to tell you. Like I just said, on my days off, I just stay home. I don't sit around analyzing if I'm feeling down or not. I just sit in my chair and keep quiet. That's about it.
Can you think of any activity or thing you used to enjoy, even a little, that you don’t seem to care about anymore—even on days when work isn’t an issue?
I don't know. I just... I don't really do much of anything anymore. I told you about church. Other than that, I just sit. There's nothing else to say about it.
Can you describe how you feel most days when you wake up, even on days when you don’t have to go to work—do you feel low, empty, or just not yourself?
I don't know. I just... wake up. I get out of bed. I don't really sit there thinking about whether I feel empty or not. It's just morning.
On days when you don’t have to go to work, do you still find yourself feeling sad, hopeless, or tearful for most of the day, even if there’s no immediate stressor like work?
No. I don't sit around crying. I just... get through the day. Like I said, I'm just in my chair. I don't really pay attention to all these emotions you keep asking about.
Do you feel tired or run down most days, even on days when you don’t have to go to work or face any particular stressors?
Not particularly. I mean... I'm not doing much, so there's nothing to be tired from. I just sit.
Can you think of any time recently when you felt any pleasure or interest in something, even a little bit, outside of work?
I don't know. I guess not really. I just... I don't really look for things to be interested in. I just watch whatever's on the TV. It passes the time.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy or care about things in your life the way you used to, even things that used to make you happy?
I don't really think about it like that. I just... I don't know. I'm just getting by, I suppose. It's not about caring or not caring. It just is what it is.
Have you noticed that you don't enjoy or care about things in your life the way you used to, even things that used to make you happy?
I think you just asked me that... I don't really know what else to tell you. Like I said, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I just do what I need to do every day, and that's about it.
Can you remember if there was something you used to look forward to or enjoy doing, even a little bit, that you don’t seem to care about anymore?
I can't think of anything. Everything is just... the same, really. I don't know what else to say about it.
Can you remember if there was something you used to enjoy doing, even a little, that you don’t seem to care about anymore?
Doc... you keep asking me the exact same question. I don't know what you want me to tell you. No. There's nothing like that. I just do my job and go home. That's really all there is to it.
Have you noticed that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in just about everything, even things you used to do regularly, not just work or church?

I don't... look, you're asking the same thing again. I already told you, no. I haven't lost interest in everything. I just... I do my job, I come home. That's it. I don't know why we keep going in circles with this.
Have you noticed that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in just about everything, even things you used to do regularly, not just work or church?
I... I don't know how else to say this. We're just repeating the same thing. No, I haven't lost interest in everything. I don't... I just don't have anything else to add to that.
Looking back over the past few weeks, have you noticed that you don’t enjoy or take interest in things you used to, even a little bit—like hobbies, TV shows, or time with family?

I... doc, please. We've been over this. I don't know why you keep asking me the same question over and over. I told you... no. I haven't lost interest in everything. I just go to work and I come home. That's all. I really don't have anything else to say about it.
Looking back over the past few weeks, have you found that you don’t enjoy or take interest in most activities, even ones you used to like—even just a little bit?

Look... I don't know what you want me to say. You're asking the exact same thing again. The answer is still no. I haven't lost interest in everything. I just... I do my shift, and I rest. Can we please just move on from this?
